THERANOS '97 INVESTOR PROPOSAL (2006, Pre-IPO Transaction, $30M raise)
Mission: Make actionable health information accessible to people everywhere at the time it matters, enabling early detection and intervention of disease.
The Problem
 Adverse drug reactions cost the pharmaceutical industry billions annually. Current blood testing requires large samples, centralized labs, and 24-72 hour turnaround times. Clinical and preclinical trials are slowed by inability to monitor drug levels in real time, increasing trial costs by an estimated 20-30%.
The Solution
 Theranos has developed proprietary technology to run hundreds of laboratory tests from a few drops of blood collected via fingerstick, with results in under an hour. The system enables real-time PK/PD monitoring for drug trials, allowing dose adjustments based on live patient data. Testing costs are 20-30% lower than traditional labs with 70% margins.
The Technology
 The Theranos system uses miniaturized cartridges processed by a reader device connected to a central server. The server performs all computation, calibrating chemistry and deriving results from signal measurements. Accuracy is comparable to gold standard laboratory methods. The technology is proprietary, patented, and difficult to replicate '97 representing a significant moat.
The Business Model
 Primary market: pharmaceutical clinical and preclinical trials ($39B Phase IV market, $10B preclinical market). Value proposition to pharma: remove black box warnings, improve compound labeling, increase patient adherence, reduce trial costs 20-30%. Information fee model with 70% margins. Secondary market: consumer diagnostics via retail partnerships.
Traction
 Existing signed deals with pharmaceutical partners. Revenue projections in deck. Pre-IPO transaction '97 company expected to go public within 2 years. Current investors include Larry Ellison and Victor Palmieri.
Why Us
 First mover advantage. Technology complexity creates high barrier to entry. Existing customer base in pharma. Strong advisory board. Management culture focused on quality and execution. Technology validated against gold standard methods in internal studies.
The Ask
 $30M pre-IPO transaction. Funds will expand production capacity and business infrastructure. Open to existing and new investors.

assumption_map.grounded_in: Accuracy is comparable to gold standard laboratory methods. The technology is proprietary, patented, and difficult to replicate

assumption_map.assumption: The 70% margin projection is achievable and financially coherent given the stated 20-30% cost reduction to customers, implying the underlying unit economics support both price discount and high profitability simultaneously.
assumption_map.grounded_in: Testing costs are 20-30% lower than traditional labs with 70% margins.

assumption_map.assumption: The existing signed pharmaceutical deals constitute real, revenue-generating commercial validation of the technology's fitness for regulated clinical trial use.
assumption_map.grounded_in: Existing signed deals with pharmaceutical partners. Revenue projections in deck.

assumption_map.assumption: The company can operate its diagnostic testing system without clearing the standard regulatory pathways that govern laboratory-developed tests and medical devices, or has a viable path through them.
assumption_map.grounded_in: The Theranos system uses miniaturized cartridges processed by a reader device connected to a central server. The server performs all computation, calibrating chemistry and deriving results

assumption_map.assumption: The $30M raise is sized appropriately to achieve the stated milestone of an IPO within two years, covering both production capacity expansion and the business infrastructure required to scale.
assumption_map.grounded_in: Pre-IPO transaction — company expected to go public within 2 years. Funds will expand production capacity and business infrastructure.

objections.title: Technology Validity Rests on Unverifiable Internal Claims
objections.grounded_in: Accuracy is comparable to gold standard laboratory methods. The technology is proprietary, patented, and difficult to replicate
objections.objection: The sole evidence offered for the system's analytical accuracy is internal validation studies — conducted by the same organization selling the technology. No independent third-party laboratory, academic institution, or regulatory body has confirmed that fingerstick-derived microsamples processed through this architecture produce clinically reliable results across hundreds of assay types.
objections.challenge: The proposal uses the technology's proprietary opacity — framed as a competitive moat — to simultaneously justify why independent verification hasn't happened and why it isn't needed. This is a circular structure: the secrecy that prevents replication also prevents scrutiny. In a diagnostic context, where results will inform dosing decisions in human clinical trials, internal validation is not a substitute for external replication. If the accuracy claim fails under independent review, the entire value proposition to pharma, the margin structure, and the IPO thesis collapse simultaneously.

objections.title: Regulatory Pathway for Diagnostic Use Is Entirely Absent
objections.grounded_in: The Theranos system uses miniaturized cartridges processed by a reader device connected to a central server. The server performs all computation, calibrating chemistry and deriving results from signal measurements.
objections.objection: The proposal describes a device-plus-software architecture that processes human blood samples to produce clinical results, which falls squarely within FDA jurisdiction as either a medical device or a laboratory-developed test — yet the document contains no mention of FDA clearance, 510(k) submission, CLIA certification, or any regulatory engagement whatsoever.
objections.challenge: This is not a peripheral compliance detail. Diagnostic tests used in pharmaceutical clinical trials operate under strict FDA oversight, and results that inform drug dosing in human subjects require a demonstrated regulatory basis. The secondary market — consumer diagnostics via retail partnerships — adds a second, equally demanding regulatory layer. A $30M raise intended to scale production capacity and infrastructure into a market the company cannot legally serve without regulatory clearance is not a growth plan; it is a deployment of capital ahead of an unresolved existential gate. The absence of any regulatory discussion in the proposal is itself the most important signal in the document.

objections.title: Traction Claims Are Asserted, Not Evidenced
objections.grounded_in: Existing signed deals with pharmaceutical partners. Revenue projections in deck. Current investors include Larry Ellison and Victor Palmieri.
objections.objection: The traction section offers signed deals, unnamed partners, and investor name-drops as proxies for commercial validation — none of which confirm that the technology has been used to generate real diagnostic results in a live trial context. 'Signed deals' could represent letters of intent, pilot agreements, or feasibility contracts that impose no obligation to use Theranos data for actual clinical decisions.
objections.challenge: The distinction matters precisely because this is a pre-IPO transaction where the implied narrative is that commercial momentum is established and the raise is for scaling, not for proving. If the signed deals do not represent recurring, data-reliant revenue from ongoing trials, the $39B Phase IV market sizing and the revenue projections in the deck are disconnected from demonstrated demand. Investor identity — Ellison, Palmieri — speaks to fundraising skill, not product performance. A new investor cannot independently verify any of the traction claims as presented, which means they are being asked to price a $30M check against asserted, unauditable momentum.

assumption_map.grounded_in: Accuracy is comparable to gold standard laboratory methods. The technology is proprietary, patented, and difficult to replicate

assumption_map.assumption: The 70% margin structure is achievable and internally consistent with the claimed 20-30% cost reduction versus traditional labs — both can be true simultaneously at the proposed price points.

objections.title: Core Technology Accuracy Is Unverified by Any Independent Party
objections.grounded_in: Accuracy is comparable to gold standard laboratory methods. The technology is proprietary, patented, and difficult to replicate
objections.objection: The proposal asserts accuracy parity with gold-standard methods but cites only 'internal studies' as validation — meaning the single most load-bearing technical claim in the entire document has never been tested by anyone without a direct financial interest in the outcome.
objections.challenge: For a diagnostic device, accuracy is not a feature claim — it is the product. Every downstream value proposition (removing black box warnings, real-time PK/PD monitoring, consumer diagnostics) collapses entirely if the test results are unreliable. The fact that the technology is 'proprietary and difficult to replicate' is presented as a moat, but it simultaneously makes independent verification structurally impossible for any investor conducting due diligence. You are being asked to commit $30M to a device whose core performance claim cannot be checked.

objections.title: Margin and Pricing Claims Are Arithmetically Irreconcilable
objections.grounded_in: Testing costs are 20-30% lower than traditional labs with 70% margins
objections.objection: The proposal simultaneously claims that Theranos undercuts traditional lab pricing by 20-30% and operates at 70% gross margins — two figures that, taken together, imply traditional labs operate at margins near or above 90%, which is not consistent with the economics of the laboratory diagnostics industry.
objections.challenge: Quest Diagnostics and Laboratory Corporation of America, the dominant incumbents, operate at gross margins in the 35-45% range. If Theranos prices 20-30% below them and still achieves 70% margins, the implied cost structure requires a cost-of-goods reduction so dramatic it would itself be the headline technological claim of this proposal — yet it is stated as a footnote with no supporting breakdown. Either the margin figure is wrong, the pricing discount is wrong, or the cost reduction mechanism is unsubstantiated. Any of these three possibilities materially misrepresents the financial model being sold to investors.

objections.title: Traction Claims Are Asserted Without Any Verifiable Evidence
objections.grounded_in: Existing signed deals with pharmaceutical partners. Revenue projections in deck.
objections.objection: The proposal references 'existing signed deals' and 'revenue projections' without naming a single pharmaceutical partner, disclosing contract values, or providing audited financials — leaving every traction claim entirely unverifiable at the moment of the investment decision.
objections.challenge: 'Signed deals' without named counterparties, disclosed terms, or recognized revenue cannot be distinguished from letters of intent, pilot agreements with no minimum commitments, or arrangements that are contingent on performance milestones the technology may not yet meet. Current investors Larry Ellison and Victor Palmieri are named as social proof, but investor identity does not validate commercial traction. A $30M pre-IPO commitment is being solicited on the basis of revenue evidence that is explicitly deferred to a deck — which itself contains projections, not actuals.

objections.title: Regulatory Pathway for Multi-Test Diagnostic Device Is Entirely Absent
objections.grounded_in: Funds will expand production capacity and business infrastructure.
objections.objection: The proposal allocates $30M to scaling production and infrastructure but contains no mention of FDA clearance, CLIA certification, or any regulatory status for a device that runs hundreds of diagnostic tests from a novel sample collection method — an absence that is not an oversight but a foundational gap.
objections.challenge: A fingerstick-based device replacing venous draws across hundreds of assay types sits squarely within FDA oversight under 21 CFR Part 820 and requires either 510(k) clearance or PMA approval for each test category, in addition to CLIA compliance for the laboratory operations. The consumer diagnostics channel referenced as a secondary market amplifies this exposure further. Expanding production capacity before regulatory clearance is confirmed means the $30M could be deployed into infrastructure that cannot legally operate at scale in its target markets. The proposal treats regulation as if it does not exist.

assumption_map.assumption: The Theranos system can actually perform hundreds of laboratory tests accurately from a fingerstick blood sample — the entire value proposition depends on this being technically real and validated.
assumption_map.grounded_in: "Accuracy is comparable to gold standard laboratory methods. The technology is proprietary, patented, and difficult to replicate."

assumption_map.assumption: The 70% margin business model is achievable at scale, meaning the cost structure claimed — tests running at 20-30% below traditional lab pricing while maintaining 70% margins — is internally consistent and operationally sustainable.
assumption_map.grounded_in: "Testing costs are 20-30% lower than traditional labs with 70% margins. Information fee model with 70% margins."

assumption_map.assumption: Pharmaceutical clinical trial partners will adopt and rely on Theranos data for regulatory submissions, meaning the technology either has or can obtain the necessary regulatory clearances to be used in FDA-governed trial contexts.
assumption_map.grounded_in: "Primary market: pharmaceutical clinical and preclinical trials ($39B Phase IV market, $10B preclinical market). Value proposition to pharma: remove black box warnings, improve compound labeling."

assumption_map.assumption: The 'existing signed deals with pharmaceutical partners' constitute genuine, revenue-generating commercial relationships that independently validate market demand — not letters of intent, pilots, or internally characterized agreements.
assumption_map.grounded_in: "Existing signed deals with pharmaceutical partners. Revenue projections in deck. Current investors include Larry Ellison and Victor Palmieri."

assumption_map.assumption: The IPO timeline is credible — the company is 2 years from public markets, implying the business has the financial maturity, audited performance, and regulatory standing to withstand public market scrutiny.
assumption_map.grounded_in: "Pre-IPO transaction — company expected to go public within 2 years."

objections.title: Technology Validation Is Entirely Self-Reported
objections.grounded_in: "Accuracy is comparable to gold standard laboratory methods. The technology is proprietary, patented, and difficult to replicate."
objections.objection: The only evidence offered that the technology works is the company's own assertion — 'validated against gold standard methods in internal studies' is not independent validation, it is the company marking its own homework.
objections.challenge: The proprietary and difficult-to-replicate nature of the technology, cited here as a moat, functions equally as a shield against external scrutiny. At $30M and a claimed IPO trajectory, the absence of any third-party analytical validation — from academic labs, reference laboratory partners, or regulatory bodies — is not a gap in the deck; it is the central question the deck refuses to answer. An investor cannot distinguish a working system from a non-working one on the basis of this document alone.

objections.title: Regulatory Pathway for Pharma Use Is Absent
objections.grounded_in: "Value proposition to pharma: remove black box warnings, improve compound labeling, increase patient adherence, reduce trial costs 20-30%."
objections.objection: Using novel diagnostic data to influence compound labeling and black box warning decisions places Theranos squarely inside FDA-regulated clinical trial infrastructure — yet the proposal contains zero discussion of regulatory clearance, CLIA certification, or FDA submission status.
objections.challenge: Pharma companies cannot legally substitute an uncleared diagnostic instrument for validated assays in submissions to the FDA without triggering regulatory exposure of their own. If Theranos lacks CLIA certification and FDA 510(k) or PMA clearance for its specific assays, the entire primary market thesis collapses — pharmaceutical partners would be adopting a tool that could invalidate their trial data or expose them to regulatory liability. The silence on this point at HIGH stakes is not an oversight; it is the most important missing fact in the document.

objections.title: Margin Claims Are Arithmetically Incoherent
objections.grounded_in: "Testing costs are 20-30% lower than traditional labs with 70% margins."
objections.objection: Claiming simultaneously that prices are 20-30% below market and that margins are 70% requires the underlying cost structure to be dramatically lower than incumbent labs — a claim that is asserted but never supported with any unit economics, cost breakdown, or manufacturing data.
objections.challenge: Traditional reference laboratories operating at scale — Quest, LabCorp — achieve margins in the 15-25% range. For Theranos to price 20-30% below them while reporting 70% margins, their cost-per-test would need to be roughly one-fifth of incumbent cost structures. This would represent not an incremental improvement but a complete reinvention of laboratory economics. No manufacturing cost data, reagent sourcing, cartridge bill-of-materials, or labor model is provided to support this figure. The 70% margin claim is load-bearing for the entire investment thesis and is currently a number without a foundation.

objections.title: Traction Claims Are Unverifiable as Stated
objections.grounded_in: "Existing signed deals with pharmaceutical partners. Revenue projections in deck. Current investors include Larry Ellison and Victor Palmieri."
objections.objection: The traction section conflates investor brand names with customer validation — the presence of Larry Ellison as an investor says nothing about whether pharmaceutical partners are generating revenue or whether 'signed deals' represent binding purchase commitments.
objections.challenge: The document does not name a single pharmaceutical partner, disclose deal terms, provide revenue figures, or distinguish between signed contracts, letters of intent, and pilot agreements. 'Revenue projections in deck' defers to a document not under review. At a $30M ask with a 2-year IPO claim, an investor requires auditable evidence of commercial traction — not a reference to projections and a roster of co-investors. The structure of this section is designed to imply validation while providing none that can be independently confirmed.
